solutions.latex:
This is a geometric progression where $a=8$ and $r=5$.

1 million unique views require finding the sum of the geometric progression.

$$\begin{aligned}S_n&=\dfrac{a(r^n-1)}{r-1}\\ 1000000&=\dfrac{8(5^n-1)}{4}\\ 1000000&=2(5^n-1)\\ 5^n-1&=500000\\ 5^n&=5000001\\ n\ln 5&=\ln 5000001\\ n&=\dfrac{\ln 5000001}{\ln 5}\\ &=8.1533\ldots\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, it takes 9 full days to reach 1 million unique views.

Marker's notes: Many students used $T_n$ rather than $S_n$. 2 marks were awarded if $T_n$ was used. Coincidently using $T_n$ produces the same answer.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: Correctly determines the number of days after solving the geometric progression equation using logarithm laws; 2: Correctly solves the required equation using logarithm laws or equivalent effort; 1: Identifies that a sum of a geometric progression is required and obtains the equation $1000000=\dfrac{8(5^n-1)}{4}$ or equivalent

solutions.latex:
Horizontal asymptote is at $y=\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}f(x)$.

$$\begin{aligned}y&=\lim_{x\to\infty}f(x)\\ &=\lim_{x\to\infty}\dfrac{2x^2}{x^2-4}\\ &=\lim_{x\to\infty}\dfrac{\frac{2x^2}{x^2}}{\frac{x^2}{x^2}-\frac{4}{x^2}}\\ &=\lim_{x\to\infty}\dfrac{2}{1-\frac{4}{x^2}}\\ &=\dfrac{2}{1-0}\\ &=2\end{aligned}$$

Marker's notes: All students were given a mark for this question due to its difficulty and vagueness of the syllabus.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: Correctly uses limits to show that the horizontal asymptote is at $y=2$

$$\begin{aligned}x^2-4&=0\\ x^2&=4\\ x&=\pm2\end{aligned}$$

solutions.latex:
Team B is more successful at scoring goals as each value in its 5-point summary is higher than Team A’s equivalent value.

Note:

\begin{itemize}
\item Students needed to select only reasoning that supported Team B being more successful and state that, not additional information even if correct e.g. Team B being slightly positively skewed or symmetrical.
\item Question stated use summary statistics.
\item correct terminology was required, for example median, not med and correct percentages needed to be quoted.
\item the justification required correct context – scores given were match scores. If referring to the percentage of scores, it needed to be in this context e.g. Team B scored greater than 27 goals in 50% of matches.
\item Stating Team B has a higher interquartile range or larger range does not justify higher scores. Consider a team with $Q_1=10$ and $Q_3=20$ or lowest and highest scores 8 and 23.
\item Reasoning had to be supported by the data. Team B having a higher median is proved by the data. Team B having a higher mean is not. The summary statistics you use should be supported by the data.
\item Students who gave more than one reason required both to be correct to get the mark (e.g. in multiple choice can not give the correct plus an incorrect answer and get the mark.
\end{itemize}
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: justification which includes correct terminology and reference to at least one of the quartiles or median without additional information not supporting the correct solution

$\therefore\sin x=\dfrac{-1}{2}$, $\sin x=2$ (not a solution, $-1\le\sin x\le1$)

$$\begin{aligned}p(x)&=\int-0.015e^{-0.01x}\,dx\\ &=-0.015\int e^{-0.01x}\,dx\\ &=\dfrac{-0.015}{-0.01}e^{-0.01x}+c\\ p(x)&=1.5e^{-0.01x}+c\end{aligned}$$

We know that \$2.35 is the price per tube for 50 tubes per week.

$$\begin{aligned}p(50)&=1.5e^{-0.01(50)}+c\\ 2.35&=1.5e^{-0.01(50)}+c\\ c&=2.35-0.91=1.44\end{aligned}$$

$$\therefore p(x)=1.5e^{-0.01x}+1.44$$

Note:

A lot of students incorrectly divided 2.35 by $\dfrac{3}{2}$ or 1.5 after substitution.

Some incorrectly substituted the values for $x$ and $p(x)$.

solutions.latex:
$$\begin{aligned}\int_{\frac{3}{2}}^{k}6x^2-4x^3\,dx&=-\dfrac{27}{16}\\ \Big[2x^3-x^4\Big]_{\frac{3}{2}}^{k}&=-\dfrac{27}{16}\\ \left[2k^3-k^4\right]-\left[2\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^3-\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^4\right]&=-\dfrac{27}{16}\\ 2k^3-k^4-\dfrac{27}{4}+\dfrac{81}{16}&=-\dfrac{27}{16}\\ 2k^3-k^4&=0\\ k^3(2-k)&=0\\ k=0\quad&\text{or}\quad k=2\end{aligned}$$

$\therefore k=2\quad\left(k>\dfrac{3}{2}\right)$

Notes;

Overall very poorly done.

Many students did not recognise that the integral should equal to a negative value as the area is below the x-axis.

Many did absolute the integral, however then were not able to solve correctly to get final answer.

Method 2:

Was to set up and solve

$$\int_0^k 6x^2-4x^3\,dx=0$$

Recognising that the integral above and below show add to give 0.

solutions.latex:
Applying Pythagoras Theorem in right-angled traingle $\Delta PQR$

$$\begin{aligned}(PQ)^2&=(QR)^2+(PR)^2\\ (5-x)^2&=(x)^2+(h)^2\\ h^2&=(5-x)^2-x^2\\ h^2&=25-10x+x^2-x^2\\ h^2&=25-10x\\ h&=\sqrt{25-10x}\end{aligned}$$

Area of triangle $\Delta PQR$

$$\begin{aligned}A&=\dfrac{1}{2}\times x\times\sqrt{25-10x}\\ A&=\dfrac{1}{2}x\sqrt{25-10x}\end{aligned}$$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: Correctly determining the length of PR (height h) in terms of x by applying the Pythagoras theorem, and showing the steps required for full simplification of this expression; correctly substituting the base and height into the formula for the area of a triangle and simplifying to obtain the required expression in the form given in the question; 1: Correctly identifying and setting up the relationship for the height PR but not showing the steps required for the full simplification, or making a minor error in determining the height but substituting their expression into the area formula

solutions.latex:
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\dfrac{1}{2}x\sqrt{25-10x}\\ \dfrac{dA}{dx}&=\dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{25-10x}+\dfrac{1}{2}x\times\dfrac{1}{2}(25-10x)^{1-\frac{1}{2}}(-10)\\ \dfrac{dA}{dx}&=\dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{25-10x}-\dfrac{5}{2}x\times(25-10x)^{-\frac{1}{2}}\\ \dfrac{dA}{dx}&=\dfrac{\sqrt{25-10x}}{2}-\dfrac{5x}{2\sqrt{25-10x}}\\ \dfrac{dA}{dx}&=\dfrac{25-10x-5x}{2\sqrt{25-10x}}\\ \dfrac{dA}{dx}&=\dfrac{25-15x}{2\sqrt{25-10x}}\end{aligned}$$

$\dfrac{dA}{dx}=0$ for stationary points

$$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{25-15x}{2\sqrt{25-10x}}&=0\\ 25-15x&=0\quad\text{for } 0\le x\le2.5\\ x&=\dfrac{25}{15}=\dfrac{5}{3}\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & 1 & \dfrac{5}{3} & 2\\ \hline \dfrac{dA}{dx} & 1.290994\ldots & 0 & -1.118033\ldots\\ \hline\end{array}$$

$\therefore x=\dfrac{5}{3}$ is a maximum turning point and gives maximum Area.

Maximum Area $A=\dfrac{1}{2}x\sqrt{25-10x}$

$$\begin{aligned}A&=\dfrac{1}{2}\times\dfrac{5}{3}\times\sqrt{25-10\times\dfrac{5}{3}}\\ A&=\dfrac{5}{6}\sqrt{\dfrac{75-50}{3}}\\ A&=\dfrac{5}{6}\sqrt{\dfrac{25}{3}}\\ A&=\dfrac{25}{6\sqrt{3}}\,u^2\end{aligned}$$
